Types of cancer
❖ Benign tumors (良性肿瘤) are not cancers; malignant tumors (恶性肿瘤)
are cancers.
❖ Some types of cancer are classified for the morphology (size and shape)
of the cells, such as “giant cell carcinoma”, “spindle cell carcinoma” and
“non-small cell lung cancer”.
https://www.verywellhealth.com/

考

❖ Initiation → Promotion → Progression

Cancer initiation is a rare event
❖ The completion of the initiation of carcinogenesis would be a very
考
rare event without: loss of capacity to repair genetic errors,
leading to an increased mutation and genomic instability, thus
accelerating all the other changes.
Signal Transduct. Target. Ther., 2024, 9(1)

Mechanisms of cancer initiation
❖ Pathophysiological mechanism of cancer:
考
❑ DNA damage:
▪ DNA damage is the primary cause of cancer;
▪ Causes: endogenous (metabolites, reactive oxygen species……)
and exogenous (UV, aflatoxins, infection……);
▪ DNA damage is an abnormal structure in DNA, while a mutation
is a change in the sequence of base pairs (not all DNA damages
induce mutation; not all mutations caused by DNA damage);
▪ DNA damage induces DNA damage response (DDR);
▪ The process of DNA damage induces cancer:

Chemotherapy is systemic
❖ Chemotherapy is one of the major categories of the medical discipline
specifically for cancer, which is called medical oncology (肿瘤内科).
❖ Chemotherapy (whether classic chemotherapy, hormonal therapy, or
targeted therapy) is systemic (therapeutics are introduced into the blood
stream and therefore can treat cancer anywhere in the body); local
therapy (surgery, radiotherapy, and laser therapy) only works where the
treatments are applied.
❖ Limitations: chemotherapy does not always work, and even when it is
useful, it may not completely destroy the cancer:
❑ Side effects;
❑ Resistance;
❑ Combination.

Efficacy and dosage
❖ The chemotherapy efficacy depends on the type and the stage of cancer.
❖ Curative (e.g., some leukemias), ineffective (e.g., some brain cancers),
needless (e.g., some skin cancers).
❖ Dosage of chemotherapy can be difficult: too low → ineffective against
the cancer; too high → intolerable toxicity.
❖ The standard method of determining chemotherapy dosage is based on
calculated body surface area (BSA).
❑ Only considering body weight and height;
❑ Other factors may influence
drug absorption: age, sex,
organ function, metabolism,
PK variation, obesity……

Antimetabolites
❖ Antimetabolites interfere with the biosynthesis of nucleic acid and
考
therefore inhibit cell division and tumor growth. Because cancer
cells spend more time dividing than normal cells, inhibiting cell
division harms cancer cells more than normal cells.
❖ Antimetabolites generally impair DNA replication machinery, either by
incorporation of chemically altered nucleotides or by depleting the
supply of deoxynucleotides.
❖ Usually CCSA (S phase).
❖ Types:
❑ Base analogues;
❑ Nucleoside analogues;
❑ Nucleotide analogues;
❑ Antifolates;
❑ Others.

Alkylating agents
❖ Alkylating agents (烷化剂) attach alkyl groups to DNA.
考
❖ Cancer cells proliferate faster and with less error-correcting than
normal cells, they are more sensitive to DNA damage (alkylated).
❖ Alkylating agents are also toxic to normal cells, most of them are also
carcinogenic.

Antimicrotubule agents
❖ Also called mitotic inhibitor, usually are plant-derived alkaloids that
考

❖ Stabilizers (inhibiting depolymerization of α/β-tubulin) and
destabilizers (inhibiting polymerization of α/β-tubulin);
❖ CCSA (M phase).
❖ Three major classes: Taxane family (紫杉烷类), Colchicine analogues
(秋水仙碱类), and Vinca alkaloids (长春花碱类).

Tyrosine kinase inhibitors
❖ Tyrosine kinases are enzymes that can transfer a phosphate group from
ATP to the tyrosine residues of specific proteins inside a cell.
❖ They functions as an "on" or "off" switch in many cellular functions. They
can become mutated, stuck in the "on" position, and cause unregulated
growth of the cell, which is necessary for the cancer development.
❖ Receptor tyrosine kinases and non-receptor tyrosine kinases.
Oncogene, 2021, 40(24)

Non-receptor tyrosine kinase inhibitors
❖ Target: Bcr-Abl fusion protein (“Philadelphia chromosome”).
考
❖ Drug: Imatinib (伊马替尼), trade name Glivec® (格列卫):
❑ Binding close to the ATP binding site of Abl, locking it in a closed
conformation, and therefore inhibiting the enzyme activity;
❑ Can target other tyrosine kinases such as c-KIT and FLT3;
❑ Applications: chronic myelogenous leukemia (慢性粒细胞白血病), Ph+
acute lymphocytic leukemia (费城染色体阳性急性淋巴细胞白血病)……

Apoptosis pathway
❖ Programmed cell death (PCD) is a biological process that occurs when a
cell dies as a result of internal events, such as apoptosis (凋亡) or
autophagy (自噬).
❖ Biochemical events of apoptosis lead to characteristic cell morphological
changes (include blebbing, cell shrinkage, nuclear and DNA
fragmentation, chromatin condensation, and mRNA decay) and death.
❖ In contrast to non-programmed necrosis, apoptosis is a highly regulated
and controlled process that confers advantages.
❖ Insufficient apoptosis results in uncontrolled
cell proliferation, such as cancer.
❖ Some factors like Fas receptors and caspases
promote apoptosis; while some factors such as
the Bcl-2 family members inhibit apoptosis.
❖ Induce apoptosis is a popular strategy for
cancer treatment.

Combination therapy
❖ The combination of anti-cancer drugs enhances efficacy because it
targets key pathways in a characteristically synergistic or an additive
manner. This approach potentially reduces drug resistance, while
simultaneously providing therapeutic benefits.
Nat. Rev. Drug

Immunotherapy
❖ Cancer immunotherapy (immuno-oncotherapy) stimulates and improves
the natural ability of immune system to treat cancer;
❖ Can be classified as two categorizes:
❑ Active therapies (e.g., cancer vaccines, CAR-T……);
❑ Passive therapies (e.g., cytokine therapy, checkpoint inhibition……);

Immunotherapy - CAR-T
❖ Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) are engineered receptor proteins to
give T cells the new ability to target a specific cancer antigen and activate
T cell responses.
❖ Approved: e.g., Axicabtagene ciloleucel 阿基仑赛 (Yescarta® 奕凯达).
Credit @ Associated Press Credit @ Carl June’s Lab

Immunotherapy - checkpoint inhibition
❖ Immune checkpoints are regulators of the immune system, they are
crucial for self-tolerance, which prevents the immune system from
attacking cells indiscriminately.
❖ Some cancers can protect themselves by stimulating immune checkpoint
targets → checkpoint inhibitors (e.g., Ipilimumab, 易普利单抗).
Nat. Rev. Dis. Primers, 2020, 6(1)
